problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a circuit of 10 distribution centers across a region, with the following site coordinates (in miles):

Center P: Coordinates (76,163)  
Center Q: Coordinates (90,21)  
Center R: Coordinates (63,113)  
Center S: Coordinates (161,94)  
Center T: Coordinates (163,135)  
Center U: Coordinates (14,96)  
Center V: Coordinates (104,2)  
Center W: Coordinates (106,186)  
Center X: Coordinates (82,112)  
Center Y: Coordinates (52,95)

The travel distances between centers, measured in miles, are precisely as follows:

P to R: 51.7 miles  
P to S: 109.5 miles  
P to T: 91.4 miles  
P to U: 91.3 miles  
P to V: 163.4 miles  
P to W: 37.8 miles  
P to X: 51.4 miles  
P to Y: 72.1 miles  
Q to R: 95.9 miles  
Q to S: 101.8 miles  
Q to T: 135.4 miles  
Q to U: 106.8 miles  
Q to V: 23.6 miles  
Q to W: 165.8 miles  
Q to X: 91.4 miles  
Q to Y: 83.2 miles  
R to S: 99.8 miles  
R to T: 102.4 miles  
R to U: 51.9 miles  
R to V: 118.3 miles  
R to W: 84.7 miles  
R to X: 19.0 miles  
R to Y: 21.1 miles  
S to T: 41.0 miles  
S to U: 147.0 miles  
S to V: 108.2 miles  
S to W: 107.2 miles  
S to X: 81.0 miles  
S to Y: 109.0 miles  
T to U: 154.0 miles  
T to V: 145.5 miles  
T to W: 76.5 miles  
T to X: 84.2 miles  
T to Y: 118.0 miles  
U to V: 130.1 miles  
U to W: 128.7 miles  
U to X: 69.9 miles  
U to Y: 38.0 miles  
V to W: 184.0 miles  
V to X: 112.2 miles  
V to Y: 106.6 miles  
W to X: 77.8 miles  
W to Y: 105.8 miles  
X to Y: 34.5 miles

Due to infrastructure limitations, there is no direct route available between Center P and Center Q. Furthermore, operational requirements dictate that exactly one of two specific connections must be incorporated into the circuit: either the route between Center Q and Center R, or the route between Center R and Center S.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed loop that visits every distribution center exactly once before returning to the point of origin.
